extraction.name: RoboFAC dataset
extraction.description: A large-scale and diverse robotic failure QA dataset with 9,440 erroneous manipulation trajectories and 78,623 QA pairs across diverse tasks and scenes in simulation and real-world environments.
extraction.creator: Weifeng Lu; Minghao Ye; Zewei Ye; Ruihan Tao; Shuo Yang; Bo Zhao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected from both simulation and real-world robotic tasks. In simulation, data were collected for 14 tasks in ManiSkill with added objects and scenes, generating erroneous trajectories by replacing expert policy code with error-inducing snippets and recording each failure video with descriptive text. In the real world, data were collected for 6 tasks via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm, with each video accompanied by textual description.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Experiments, Software Collection, Direct measurement, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Robot manipulation videos and corresponding textual descriptions from simulated and real-world executions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors manually cleaned the collected simulation data and retained approximately 75% because some motion planning failures produced trajectories inconsistent with the textual descriptions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The raw videos were annotated into video-based QA samples for eight question types. Reference answers for five question types were directly extracted from the textual descriptions, while failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction answers were generated by GPT-4o using both the video and textual description, then manually reviewed and corrected.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: GPT-4o-generated annotations were manually reviewed and corrected to ensure quality.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may overfit to failure patterns, so the authors also collected successful trajectories to mitigate this.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current integration into VLA-controlled robotic systems is not yet seamless, and the work applies the model exclusively to VLA models; more natural automated correction delivery and targeted strategies for hierarchical policies remain future work.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used to train and evaluate models for robotic failure video understanding, including task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction.

name.evidence: we first construct a large-scale and diverse dataset of robotic failures ( RoboFAC dataset ) covering robotic tasks of varying complexity in both simulated and real-world environments.

description.evidence: Firstly, we construct RoboFAC dataset comprising 9,440 erroneous manipulation trajectories and 78,623 QA pairs across 16 diverse tasks and 53 scenes in both simulation and real-world environments.

url.evidence: Our model and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/MINT-SJTU/RoboFAC .

inLanguage.evidence: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently advanced robotic manipulation by translating natural-language instructions and image information into sequential control actions.

isLiveDataset.evidence: Our model and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/MINT-SJTU/RoboFAC .

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We collect the simuluation data for 14 robotic tasks in the ManiSkill environment [25], augmented with objects from the YCB Object Dataset [26] to increase object diversity and scenes from ReplicaCAD [27] and AI2-THOR [28] to enrich environmental diversity. For each custom task, we first define an expert policy by specifying target end-effector poses for each substage, and the feasible paths and trajectories for the robotic arm to reach these poses are generated using motion planning. To generate failure data, we replace the original expert policy with a code snippet that generates an erroneous trajectory at the selected substage, causing the overall robotic task to fail. Real-World Data. We collected real-world data for 6 tasks, including two tasks that are not present in the simulation dataset. Data collection is performed via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: During data collection, we record each robotic failure video along with a corresponding descriptive text. As with the simulation data, each video is accompanied by a corresponding textual description.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Given the motion planning for the robotic arm occasionally failed, resulting in trajectories that did not align with the corresponding textual descriptions, we manually performed thorough data cleaning and retained approximately 75% of the collected data.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We annotate the raw data to construct video-based QA samples corresponding to eight question types... For each sample, the reference answer is generated based on the textual description associated with the video. For five question types— task identification ,task planning ,failure detection ,failure identification , and failure locating —the reference answers can be directly extracted from the corresponding textual description... For the remaining three types— failure explanation ,high-level correction , and low-level correction —we utilize both the video and its corresponding textual description as inputs to GPT-4o to generate the reference answers. To ensure annotation quality, all outputs from GPT-4o were manually reviewed and corrected.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: To prevent models from overfitting to failure pattems, we also collect 1,160 successful trajectories from simulation and 122 successful trajectories from real-world executions.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Although we have demonstrated that the RoboFAC model’s correction suggestions can effectively assist the VLA model in recovering from failures, our current integration of the model into the VLA-controlled robotic system is not yet seamless. In future work, we aim to explore more natural and automated mechanisms for delivering correction suggestions. Moreover, apply our model exclusively to the VLA model in this work.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: Based on this dataset, we establish a comprehensive evaluation benchmark that assesses multimodal models’ capabilities in robotic failure video understanding. Leveraging the RoboFAC dataset, we build a multimodal large model ( RoboFAC model ) capable of performing robotic task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction based on robot video.
